00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: A Stranger
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Corvus Umbranox appears as the Stranger during the final Thieves Guild scene, before reclaiming his identity as the Gray Fox.
00A2A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies the final-scene Stranger as the Gray Fox himself. His reputation as the greatest of thieves and his documented spellcasting support an elite rating, but not the Gray Cowl’s supernatural curse as personal combat power.

0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Abhuki
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Khajiit innkeeper at Faregyl Inn and an advanced Alteration trainer; no combat training or combat feats are established.
0389B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies her as an ordinary adult civilian. Her advanced Alteration training role does not establish combat mastery, so the ordinary adult civilian baseline applies.

0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Name: Achille
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Description: Achille is a Breton Blade stationed at Cloud Ruler Temple, identifying him as a trained professional fighter.
0A3166:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His confirmed Blade identity supports the professional-soldier baseline; the article establishes no evidence for veteran or exceptional combat mastery.

02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A veteran Imperial Legion commander who spent forty years in service and devoted much of his career to investigating and disrupting the Dark Brotherhood.
02FB2B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His decades of service and sustained work against dangerous assassins support a seasoned-combatant rating. The article does not establish elite personal combat mastery or feats warranting a higher tier.

1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adamus Phillida's Bodyguard
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An unnamed Imperial City Watch bodyguard assigned to Adamus Phillida, sworn to protect him if threatened.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His City Watch bodyguard role supports the competent professional-soldier baseline. The article establishes his duty to defend Phillida but no exceptional combat feats.
1778DC:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article does not describe his individual combat training or feats.

01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adanrel
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adanrel is an ordinary adult Wood Elf civilian who works at the Imperial Trading Company Warehouse and describes herself as lacking skills.
01FB56:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies her as a specific civilian and provides no established combat training or exceptional feats. The ordinary adult civilian baseline is appropriate.

01681B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adeo
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dark Seducer captain who leads surviving forces at Pinnacle Rock and fights Knights and Priests of Order during the rescue of Dylora.
01681B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Adeo is an active combatant and leader in the defense of her stronghold, but the article establishes no exceptional personal feats or combat mastery.

0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adoring Fan
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf commoner who becomes the Grand Champion’s admirer; no combat training or notable martial feats are established.
0AED40:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies him as a commoner, supporting the project’s ordinary civilian baseline of limited training or modest natural threat.

02F865:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adosi Serethi
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf ostler and Aleswell resident, rendered invisible by Ancotar’s experiment; no combat training or fighting feats are established.
02F865:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies her as an ordinary adult civilian and establishes no combat training or feats, supporting the project’s Basic civilian baseline.

016057:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrian Decanius
016057:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adrian Decanius is an Imperial commoner and ordinary civilian; no combat training or notable martial ability is established.
016057:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as a commoner and lists basic weapons, but establishes no combat expertise. The ordinary adult civilian baseline is appropriate.

02950A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adrienne Berene
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Adrienne Berene is a scholarly Breton mage whose destructive magic makes her a dangerous opponent, though her documented abilities do not establish exceptional mastery.
02950A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her UESP article describes her as a mage with a particularly powerful Destruction repertoire. That supports a seasoned threat, but no distinctive combat feats or demonstrated mastery justify a higher tier.

068828:Oblivion.esm.Name: Adult Rumare Slaughterfish
068828:Oblivion.esm.Description: A mundane aquatic slaughterfish variant found around Lake Rumare; it is an animal without magical or weapon-wielding abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Its verified form supports an ordinary natural-threat rating; the source establishes no exceptional feats, training, or supernatural abilities.
068828:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source confirms the Rumare variant but gives no specific feats for this adult individual.

185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Elderly Breton fisherman injured by a slaughterfish, leaving him unable to resume fishing; no combat training or exceptional ability is established.
185FE0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His account and the article describe an old man whose injury left him too weak to collect the remaining scales. With no combat training or feats established, the frail elderly civilian baseline fits.

0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aengvir
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf commoner living in Harlun’s Watch; no combat training or unusual abilities are established.
0514C4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article confirms an ordinary civilian identity, fitting the project’s basic baseline for a mundane adult without established combat training. His quest connection flags sensitivity, not combat strength.

035726:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aenvir
035726:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Wood Elf hunter and former shop employee who participates in recurring robberies with two companions and relies on a dagger in combat.
035726:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His hunting background and participation in armed robberies show some capacity to pose a threat, but no established combat training or exceptional feats support a higher tier than a basic mortal.

098254:Oblivion.esm.Name: Afflicted Brethren
098254:Oblivion.esm.Description: A vampire and former worshipper of Azura, one of five afflicted brethren who slew the powerful vampire Dratik before contracting vampirism.
098254:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor is confirmed as a vampire, and the brethren’s shared history of slaying a powerful vampire supports competent combat capability without establishing exceptional individual mastery.

01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agarmir
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Nord thief and criminal supplier who prepares an ambush and attacks when confronted during the Unfriendly Competition quest.
01FC54:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Agarmir as an ordinary mortal thief and describes his ambush, but establishes no notable combat training or feats. The ordinary adult baseline is appropriate.

02D028:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agata
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agata is a Mages Guild Evoker who supports the Leyawiin chapter and helps with its recommendation quest.
02D028:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established role as a Guild mage supports competent magical ability, but the article gives no combat feats or combat-specific mastery to justify a higher tier.

0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnar the Unwavering
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agnar is the corpse of a Nord warrior and former Thirsk chieftain, found near Dive Rock after seeking the Uderfrykte Matron.
0C55E5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The encountered form is an unanimated corpse, so his former status as a warrior does not establish present combat capability.

028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agnete the Pickled
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord smith and proprietor of Hammer and Tongs in Skingrad, praised for her armor-repair skills; no combat training or fighting feats are established.
028F9B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her smithing and armorer skills establish craft expertise, not combat mastery. As an ordinary adult mortal without established combat training, she fits the Basic baseline.

037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Agronak gro-Malog
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Agronak gro-Malog, the Gray Prince, is a vampiric-blooded Orc and long-standing Arena Grand Champion whose unusual abilities make him an exceptionally formidable fighter.
037FF8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His nearly decade-long reign and reputation as unbeatable, alongside explicitly heightened abilities from vampiric blood, support elite combat prowess. The evidence does not establish feats warranting legendary mastery.

0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ah-Malz
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ah-Malz is an Argonian blademaster and experienced goblin hunter who regularly spars with a fellow Fighters Guild member.
0293D5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His blademaster identity, expert goblin hunting, and regular sparring support a seasoned-combatant rating, but the article establishes no exceptional feats warranting an elite tier.

034E87:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahdarji
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Description: A retired Khajiit thief with advanced Light Armor training; her history and continued guild work indicate practical combat experience, but no exceptional feats are established.
034E87:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established thief background and Light Armor training support a competent-fighter baseline. The article provides no evidence of veteran-level combat ability or mastery.

0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ahjazda
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Khajiit shopkeeper in Crucible who asks the player to gather items for her preparations against a feared coming catastrophe.
0155A0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Ahjazda as a shopkeeper and enchantress, but establishes no combat training or distinctive combat feats. The ordinary adult civilian baseline is appropriate.

0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ajum-Kajin
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Description: Ajum-Kajin is a mortal Argonian mage who uses magic in combat, but the article establishes no exceptional magical mastery or individual combat feats.
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity as a combat-using mage supports a basic threat rating. His high rank and guards do not establish personal combat strength, and no mastery is documented.
0356CD:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: His specific magical proficiency and independent combat ability are not established.

01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Akaviri Commander Mishaxhi
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Description: Mishaxhi is a Tsaesci warrior whose ghost guards the Draconian Madstone, wielding an Akaviri dai-katana and attacking intruders.
01C48D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His verified ghost form and identity as an armed warrior support the Ghost and professional-soldier baselines. His reputation as a great tactician does not by itself establish exceptional combat mastery.

03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alawen
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alawen is a Wood Elf master marksman who hunts with a bow and trains others in Marksman.
03C15F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her established mastery as a Marksman trainer supports the project's Master combat trainer baseline. The claim that she is Cyrodiil's best shot is only reported as a rumor and is not needed for this tier.

0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alberic Litte
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Breton Mages Guild associate and advanced Conjuration trainer, established as a practicing mage but with no reported exceptional combat feats.
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His guild role and advanced Conjuration instruction support competent magical ability above an untrained civilian, but the article establishes neither mastery nor exceptional combat prowess.
0222B8:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The article does not state his own Conjuration proficiency or describe combat feats.

0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aldos Othran
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dunmer farmer and bereaved alcoholic who confronts a Cheydinhal guard during Corruption and Conscience; no established combat training or notable fighting feats.
0034DE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes him as an ordinary adult civilian, not a trained fighter. His confrontation shows willingness to fight, but no demonstrated combat ability to justify a higher tier.

00A110:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aleron Loche
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Description: Aleron Loche is a Breton commoner caught in Kurdan’s hunt; he says he has never held a weapon and cannot fight.
00A110:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as an ordinary adult civilian with no established combat training, matching the project’s Basic baseline.

01D346:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alessia Ottus
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and city-guide author; no combat training or unusual combat abilities are established.
01D346:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies her as a commoner, author, wife, and mother, but establishes no combat feats or supernatural form. The ordinary adult civilian baseline fits.

035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alga
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alga is a Nord bard and Speechcraft trainer in Bruma, renowned locally for storytelling. No combat training or martial feats are established.
035EC4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She is an ordinary adult mortal with no established combat training, fitting the project's Basic civilian baseline. Storytelling and Speechcraft training do not establish combat proficiency.

01D344:Oblivion.esm.Name: Algot the Northerner
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Description: Nord bard and Imperial City civilian who does odd jobs and some adventuring; no notable combat training or feats are established.
01D344:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article mentions only a little adventuring, with no evidence of professional training or exceptional ability. The project's ordinary adult civilian baseline applies.

18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alix Lencolia
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Young Breton crusader and master Blade trainer, renowned for his sword skill and associated with the Blade Training quest.
18D2B4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies Alix as the master trainer in Blade and records other trainers calling him famous for his skill with a blade. Established mastery in a combat discipline supports Tier 6.

08595D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alonzo
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alonzo is a Redguard bandit boss who leads raids on travelers with members of the Black Bow Bandits.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His active role in bandit raids supports competent combat capability, but the article provides no evidence of veteran training or exceptional personal feats.
08595D:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The source establishes his bandit role but does not describe his individual combat skill.

031867:Oblivion.esm.Name: Aloys Bincal
031867:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial farmer and civilian settler taking refuge from nearby goblins.
031867:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Aloys as an ordinary adult farmer and establishes no combat training or fighting feats; the project's civilian baseline supports Tier 2.

01207B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Althel's Ghost
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Althel is a cursed Wood Elf scout and archer whose ghost relives Vitharn’s defense; she can fight once supplied with arrows.
01207B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her verified ghost form matches the project’s tier-3 Ghost baseline. Her scout role and archery support a competent combatant, but the article establishes no exceptional mastery or feats.

030196:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alval Uvani
030196:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Dark Elf battlemage and master of Destruction magic, Alval is a dangerous opponent with additional Mysticism and Restoration spells.
030196:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article identifies him as a master of Destruction and describes him as a formidable opponent. That established magical mastery supports Tier 6; his quest role alone does not raise the tier.

02D027:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alves Uvenim
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Description: Dark Elf alchemist and Mages Guild journeyman; a practiced researcher who advises Rosentia, with no established combat feats or combat specialization.
02D027:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her documented expertise is alchemy and research, not combat. The ordinary-adult baseline is appropriate absent evidence of combat training or demonstrated fighting ability.

08209B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Alyssa
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Alyssa was a Breton conjurer, but this Dire Warren encounter represents her corpse after a fatal fall, not her living form.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The source confirms Alyssa’s identity and conjurer background, but the represented actor is deceased; no combat tier is supported for this corpse.
08209B:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her living combat ability is not established, and should not be assigned to the corpse without supporting evidence.

0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amantius Allectus
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Description: Imperial commoner and writer whose diary describes experiments on plants; no combat training or unusual combat ability is established.
0097A5:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as an ordinary adult civilian and establishes no combat training or feats, supporting the project's Basic civilian baseline.

028E75:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ambroise Canne
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Description: A renowned Block specialist whose advanced instruction and local reputation establish him as a highly accomplished defensive combatant.
028E75:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies Ambroise as an advanced Block trainer and reports that townspeople regard his shield skill as superior to the Fighters Guild trainer’s. This supports an elite specialist rating, but not master-level combat mastery.

01207A:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amiable Fanriene
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amiable Fanriene is a highly capable Breton conjurer whose formidable spellcasting contrasts with his persistent paranoia.
01207A:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article describes him as one of the Isles’ most capable mages and details a broad repertoire of powerful spells, supporting a master-level assessment.

026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amir
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amir is a mortal Redguard assassin and worshipper of Molag Bal, encountered at the shrine during the Molag Bal quest.
026B4C:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article identifies Amir as an assassin, supporting a competent trained-fighter baseline. His quest connection warrants QuestRelated handling, but does not imply greater combat power.

03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amkaos
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amkaos is a hostile Dremora torturer in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise who carries a longsword and joins an attack on Eldamil.
03CD19:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His armed role and participation in a fight support a competent combatant rating, but the article establishes no exceptional feats or mastery.

0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amminus Gregori
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Description: Cheydinhal City Guard assigned to watch the Oblivion Gate; equipped as a guard and armed with a silver longsword.
0A369F:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity as a City Guard supports the professional-soldier baseline: a competent trained fighter. The article establishes no exceptional combat mastery or feats.

000F62:Knights.esp.Name: Amragor
000F62:Knights.esp.Description: Amragor is an adult Wood Elf healer who appears in the reconditioned Chapel of Dibella after the Knights of the Nine questline.
000F62:Knights.esp.Reason: The article establishes his identity as a healer but no combat training or exceptional combat ability. An ordinary adult baseline is appropriate; healer spells alone do not establish combat mastery.

03563B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Amusei
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Amusei is an Argonian freelance thief who later joins the Thieves Guild and serves as the Gray Fox’s messenger.
03563B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes a mortal thief but no combat training or notable fighting feats. The ordinary-adult baseline is appropriate; his later Guild rank and quest role do not establish greater combat power.

05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anaxes
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anaxes is a Xivilai lord encountered in Mankar Camoran’s Paradise, where the inhabitants have trapped him in his cave.
05E1DC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied UESP article confirms his Xivilai form. The project baseline assigns verified Xivilai tier 6; unique feats are not required.

0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancestor Guardian
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Description: A guardian summoned through the Dunmer Ancestor Guardian ability; its exact creature form is not established by the available evidence.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Manual deleveling review: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Initial balance assignment; editable after in-game testing.
0C6573:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Loaded ghost model confirms summoned ancestor spirit; ordinary ghost baseline.

05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Ghost
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable ghost variant that attacks with frost-focused magic and is described as more dangerous than a standard ghost.
05D2BC:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The verified ancient form is explicitly more formidable than the ordinary ghost baseline (tier 3), supporting a modest increase to seasoned threat.

070913:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancient Sanctified Dead
070913:Oblivion.esm.Description: An ancient ghost, a more formidable spectral variant that relies on magical attacks, particularly frost, and is more powerful than a standard ghost.
070913:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor’s identity matches the ancient ghost form. UESP describes ancient ghosts as more formidable than standard ghosts, with more powerful spells, supporting a step above the project’s ordinary ghost baseline.

02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancotar
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Description: A Mages Guild wizard and warlock whose magical research made people and creatures across a wide area invisible; he also developed a counterspell.
02F86D:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His demonstrated area-effect spellcraft and ability to devise a counterspell establish substantial magical competence. The evidence supports a seasoned mage, but not exceptional combat mastery.

01D354:Oblivion.esm.Name: Ancus Afranius
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Description: Breton bard and Thieves Guild member living in the Imperial City; no combat training or notable combat feats are established.
01D354:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article confirms Ancus is an ordinary adult mortal but establishes no combat training or meaningful combat capability. The project’s ordinary adult civilian baseline supports Tier 2.

00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andragil
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Description: Wood Elf Bravil resident and master Block trainer who tests trainees by striking them with a warhammer.
00A10B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Andragil is explicitly identified as a master trainer in Block, a combat discipline. Other expert trainers credit her instruction, and her training test demonstrates her ability to withstand a prolonged combat challenge.

0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andre Labouche
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Description: Andre is encountered already dead at the base of the cliff; his remains are a clue in The Horror of Dive Rock.
0C56E4:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The represented encounter is his corpse, not Andre alive. His spellslinging in life does not establish combat capability for the dead body.

030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Andreas Draconis
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Imperial innkeeper and Dark Brotherhood quest target; he threatens to fight when confronted, but no combat training or notable feats are established.
030FDB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as an ordinary civilian, not a trained fighter. His threat and dagger do not establish greater combat ability, so the ordinary-adult baseline fits.

07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Androcide
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Unverified creature encounter; no actor-specific UESP evidence establishes its form or capabilities.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The supplied record identifies a creature but not its species or lore. Without a verified form, no project baseline can be applied.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: The encounter identity and creature form remain unverified; no suitable actor-specific UESP article was found.
07E9BB:Oblivion.esm.DelevelingReview: Unreferenced skeleton minion record in loaded base plugin; not an active encounter.

026B36:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anedhel
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anedhel is a Wood Elf witch and devout worshipper of Clavicus Vile, found at his shrine with Ma’Raska and Gul gro-Burbog.
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes an ordinary mortal identity but gives no lore-based combat feats or demonstrated magical mastery. The basic adult-mortal baseline is appropriate.
026B36:Oblivion.esm.Uncertainty: Her witch identity is established, but the article does not describe combat training, magical mastery, or notable feats.

0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalmo
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Description: High Elf alchemist and Mages Guild Evoker who offers basic Mysticism training; no combat feats or combat-focused expertise are established.
0234BB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies Angalmo as an adult mortal but establishes no combat training or demonstrated fighting ability. Basic Mysticism training does not establish combat mastery, so the ordinary adult baseline is appropriate.

026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angalsama
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Description: Angalsama is a mortal High Elf mage and Sheogorath worshipper whose documented behavior shows madness, but no established combat training or exceptional magical mastery.
026ADB:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her identity as a mage supports modest combat capability, but the article establishes no combat feats or magical proficiency that would justify a higher tier.

01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Name: Angelie
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Description: Angelie Blakeley is a Redguard commoner living in Talos Plaza; no combat training or unusual abilities are established.
01FC51:Oblivion.esm.Reason: UESP identifies her as an ordinary adult civilian without established combat training or feats, fitting the project’s Basic baseline.

052F61:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anglor's Ghost
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anglor is the ghost of a Wood Elf conjurer from Vitharn; the article says he has no spells he can cast.
052F61:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article confirms his ghost form, supporting the project's ordinary-ghost baseline. His conjurer identity does not establish greater combat mastery, and no stronger feats are documented.

00A299:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anguilon
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Description: Anguilon is a Wood Elf pirate living in Anvil who carries an iron dagger, but no exceptional combat training or feats are established.
00A299:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His identity as an ordinary adult mortal supports the Basic baseline. Being a pirate and carrying a dagger do not, by themselves, establish seasoned combat ability.

0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antoine Branck
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Description: Antoine Branck is an ordinary Breton stablehand and farmer who carries an iron war axe; no combat training or notable fighting ability is established.
0488F3:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as a civilian horse caretaker, with no evidence of combat training or feats. The ordinary adult civilian baseline supports Tier 2.

023E36:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antoinetta Marie
023E36:Oblivion.esm.Description: A novice Dark Brotherhood assassin who trains with a dagger and has limited magical and weapon resistance.
023E36:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her assassin role and regular combat training establish capability beyond an untrained civilian, but she is described as a newcomer with no feats or evidence of seasoned skill.

067418:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antus Flonius
067418:Oblivion.esm.Description: An Imperial Fighters Guild apprentice who regularly spars and is equipped as a warrior.
067418:Oblivion.esm.Reason: His Guild training and regular sparring support a competent-fighter baseline, but the article establishes no veteran experience, exceptional mastery, or notable combat feats.

0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Name: Antus Odiil
0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Description: Antus is a hot-headed young Imperial who joins his brother and the player in defending the Odiil farm from goblins, but has little established combat experience.
0222A0:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article identifies him as a warrior and shows him fighting armed, but his brother says Antus has never faced a fight like this. The Basic tier fits his modest demonstrated capability without assuming veteran training.

00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Name: Anvil Guard
00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Description: A generic Anvil city guard serving as a soldier of the local count; a trained professional fighter.
00A0AE:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The UESP article identifies county city guards as soldiers serving their local count. The project's professional-soldier baseline supports tier 3.

01EC37:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The actor-specific article identifies him as a warrior and describes him carrying a battle axe, supporting a competent-fighter baseline. No exceptional combat feats or mastery are established.

034E67:Oblivion.esm.Name: Shomara

030FD8:Oblivion.esm.Name: Sibylla Draconis
030FD8:Oblivion.esm.Description: Hostile Imperial barbarian living in Muck Valley Cavern, devoted to the animals there and targeted by the Dark Brotherhood’s Draconis contract.
030FD8:Oblivion.esm.Reason: Her article establishes hostility but no combat training, notable feats, or exceptional abilities. Rate her as an ordinary adult combat threat at the Basic baseline.

034E6B:Oblivion.esm.Reason: She is an ordinary mortal healer with no established combat training or exceptional magical mastery. Her participation in the chapel’s defense does not establish greater individual ability.

01C458:Oblivion.esm.Reason: The article establishes no combat training or notable fighting ability. The ordinary adult civilian baseline is appropriate; Helljoint alone does not establish combat frailty.

03E92B:Oblivion.esm.Name: Sinderion

000F87:Knights.esp.Name: Sir Amiel

000FB3:Knights.esp.Name: Sir Amiel

000F6A:Knights.esp.Name: Sir Berich
